flatsky module

Flat-sky routines for simulating and analyzing small patches of sky in the flat-sky approximation.

The module is grouped into four sections:

  • Fourier grid: get_lxly(), get_lxly_az_angle(), cl_to_cl2d()

  • Filters: get_lpf_hpf(), wiener_filter()

  • Simulations: convert_eb_qu(), cl2map(), make_gaussian_realization()

  • Power spectra: radial_profile(), map2cl()

cl_to_cl2d() is referenced by misc.get_beam_dic(), which calls it only when its make_2d option is set. The remaining routines are standalone utilities that are currently not used elsewhere in this repository.

A flat-sky patch is described by mapparams = [nx, ny, dx, dy], where nx and ny are the number of pixels along each axis and dx and dy are the pixel sizes in arcmin. Multipoles follow the flat-sky convention \(\ell = \sqrt{\ell_x^2 + \ell_y^2}\), with the 2-D Fourier grid supplied by get_lxly(). Power spectra carry whatever units the input cl is given in and maps carry its square root.

flatsky.get_lxly(mapparams)

Wavenumber grids \(\ell_x\) and \(\ell_y\) for a flat-sky patch.

Parameters:

mapparams (list) – Flat-sky map geometry [nx, ny, dx, dy], where nx and ny are the pixel counts along each axis and dx and dy are the pixel sizes in arcmin. nx and ny must be integers.

Returns:

  • lx (numpy.ndarray) – Wavenumbers varying along the second axis, of shape (ny, nx).

  • ly (numpy.ndarray) – Wavenumbers varying along the first axis, of shape (ny, nx).

Notes

The grids follow numpy.fft.fftfreq() ordering, so the zero mode sits at index [0, 0] and the upper half of each axis carries negative wavenumbers.

A single pixel size is used for both axes. The unpacking binds the third and fourth entries of mapparams to the same name, so the declared dx is discarded and dy is used for both. The grid is therefore correct only for square pixels, which is what the implementation assumes throughout.

flatsky.get_lxly_az_angle(lx, ly)

Twice the azimuthal angle of each Fourier mode.

Parameters:

  • lx (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – Wavenumber grids, as returned by get_lxly().

  • ly (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – Wavenumber grids, as returned by get_lxly().

Returns:

angle (numpy.ndarray) – \(2\phi_\ell\), where \(\phi_\ell = \arctan(\ell_x / -\ell_y)\), with the same shape as the inputs.

Notes

The factor of two is included because the result is used to rotate spin-2 fields in convert_eb_qu().

flatsky.cl_to_cl2d(el, cl, mapparams)

Interpolate a 1-D power spectrum onto the 2-D flat-sky Fourier grid.

Each grid point is assigned \(C_\ell\) at \(\ell = \sqrt{\ell_x^2 + \ell_y^2}\), with \(\ell_x\) and \(\ell_y\) taken from get_lxly().

Parameters:

  • el (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – Multipoles \(\ell\) at which cl is defined. Must be strictly increasing.

  • cl (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – Power spectrum \(C_\ell\), the same length as el.

  • mapparams (list) – Flat-sky map geometry [nx, ny, dx, dy], where nx and ny are the pixel counts along each axis and dx and dy are the pixel sizes in arcmin. nx and ny must be integers. A float pixel count, which is what a plain numpy.ndarray of mapparams produces, raises inside numpy.fft.fftfreq().

Returns:

cl2d (numpy.ndarray) – Power spectrum on the 2-D grid, of shape (ny, nx).

Raises:

ValueError – If el is not strictly increasing since numpy.interp() would otherwise return silently incorrect values.

Notes

numpy.interp() clamps outside the range of el, so every grid point above max(el) is assigned cl[-1] rather than zero.

flatsky.get_lpf_hpf(mapparams, lmin_lmax, filter_type=0)

Top-hat low-pass, high-pass or band-pass filter on the 2-D Fourier grid.

Parameters:

  • mapparams (list) – Flat-sky map geometry [nx, ny, dx, dy].

  • lmin_lmax (float or collections.abc.Sequence of float) – Cutoff multipole. Must be a single value for filter_type 0 or 1, and an (lmin, lmax) pair for filter_type 2.

  • filter_type (int, optional) – 0 for low pass, 1 for high pass and 2 for band pass. Default is 0.

Returns:

fft_filter (numpy.ndarray) – Filter on the 2-D grid, of shape (ny, nx), holding one inside the pass band and zero outside.

Raises:

ValueError – If filter_type is not 0, 1 or 2, or if lmin_lmax does not have the shape that filter_type requires.

flatsky.wiener_filter(mapparams, cl_signal, cl_noise, el=None)

Wiener filter on the 2-D Fourier grid.

\[W_\ell = \frac{C_\ell^\mathrm{S}}{C_\ell^\mathrm{S} + C_\ell^\mathrm{N}}\, ,\]

with both spectra placed on the grid by cl_to_cl2d().

Parameters:

  • mapparams (list) – Flat-sky map geometry [nx, ny, dx, dy].

  • cl_signal (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – Signal power spectrum \(C_\ell^\mathrm{S}\).

  • cl_noise (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – Noise power spectrum \(C_\ell^\mathrm{N}\), the same length as cl_signal.

  • el (numpy.typing.ArrayLike, optional) – Multipoles at which both spectra are defined. Default is None, which uses np.arange(len(cl_signal)).

Returns:

wiener_filter2d (numpy.ndarray) – Filter on the 2-D grid, of shape (ny, nx), with entries between zero and one.

Notes

Modes at which signal and noise both vanish are set to zero, matching the treatment of the spectrum in make_gaussian_realization().

flatsky.convert_eb_qu(map1, map2, mapparams, eb_to_qu=1)

Rotate a pair of flat-sky polarization maps between E/B and Q/U.

The transform is a rotation by \(2\phi_\ell\) applied in Fourier space,

\[\begin{split}\begin{pmatrix} Q \\ U \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} \cos 2\phi_\ell & -\sin 2\phi_\ell \\ \sin 2\phi_\ell & \cos 2\phi_\ell \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} E \\ B \end{pmatrix}\, ,\end{split}\]

with the transpose of that matrix applied in the opposite direction. The rotation is orthogonal mode by mode, but see the note below on the Nyquist row and column.

Parameters:

  • map1 (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – The pair to rotate, E and B when eb_to_qu is set and Q and U otherwise.

  • map2 (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – The pair to rotate, E and B when eb_to_qu is set and Q and U otherwise.

  • mapparams (list) – Flat-sky map geometry [nx, ny, dx, dy].

  • eb_to_qu (int, optional) – If non-zero, rotate E/B to Q/U. Otherwise rotate Q/U to E/B. Default is 1.

Returns:

map1_mod, map2_mod (numpy.ndarray) – The rotated pair, Q and U when eb_to_qu is set and E and B otherwise.

Notes

Only the real part of the inverse transform is retained. On an even-sized grid this discards information. A pure E-mode input, and a field with no power on the Nyquist row and column, are transformed exactly.

flatsky.cl2map(mapparams, cl, el=None)

Draw a Gaussian random flat-sky map with a given power spectrum.

White noise is generated in map space and multiplied by \(\sqrt{C_\ell}\) on the Fourier grid, with a pixel-area normalization chosen so that the recovered spectrum matches the input.

Parameters:

  • mapparams (list) – Flat-sky map geometry [nx, ny, dx, dy].

  • cl (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – Power spectrum \(C_\ell\) to realize.

  • el (numpy.typing.ArrayLike, optional) – Multipoles at which cl is defined. Default is None, which uses np.arange(len(cl)).

Returns:

flatskymap (numpy.ndarray) – Realization with its mean removed.

Notes

The random field is drawn with shape (nx, ny) while the Fourier grid from get_lxly() has shape (ny, nx), so the two agree only for a square patch and a rectangular one raises ValueError.

The normalization uses a single pixel size rather than \(\sqrt{\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y}\), so for non-square pixels the amplitude differs from make_gaussian_realization() by \(\sqrt{\mathrm{d}x/\mathrm{d}y}\). Use make_gaussian_realization() for correlated fields or to apply a beam.

flatsky.make_gaussian_realization(mapparams, el, cl, cl2=None, cl12=None, bl=None, qu_or_eb='qu')

Draw one Gaussian flat-sky field or a correlated pair followed by a field of zeros.

A single field is drawn as in cl2map(). When cl2 and cl12 are supplied, a second field correlated with the first is built in Fourier space from two independent white-noise realizations,

\[\tilde{f}_2 = \tilde{g}_1 \frac{C_\ell^{12}}{\sqrt{C_\ell^{11}}} + \tilde{g}_2 \sqrt{C_\ell^{22} - \frac{(C_\ell^{12})^2}{C_\ell^{11}}}\, ,\]

so that the pair carries the requested auto and cross spectra. A third field of zeros is appended, standing for B when the pair is T and E.

Parameters:

  • mapparams (list) – Flat-sky map geometry [nx, ny, dx, dy].

  • el (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – Multipoles at which the spectra are defined.

  • cl (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – Auto spectrum of the first field, \(C_\ell^{11}\).

  • cl2 (numpy.typing.ArrayLike, optional) – Auto spectrum of the second field, \(C_\ell^{22}\). Supplying it selects the correlated branch, which also requires cl12. Default is None.

  • cl12 (numpy.typing.ArrayLike, optional) – Cross spectrum of the two fields, \(C_\ell^{12}\). Required when cl2 is given. Default is None.

  • bl (numpy.typing.ArrayLike, optional) – Beam transfer function \(B_\ell\), either 1-D over el or already on the 2-D grid, applied to the output. Default is None.

  • qu_or_eb ({'qu', 'eb'}, optional) – Whether to return T, Q, U or T, E, B. Only has an effect in the correlated branch. Default is 'qu'.

Returns:

SIM (numpy.ndarray) – A single map of shape (ny, nx) or a cube of shape (3, ny, nx) in the correlated branch, with the mean removed.

Raises:

ValueError – If qu_or_eb is neither 'qu' nor 'eb' or if cl2 is given without cl12.

Notes

The random fields are drawn with shape (nx, ny) while the Fourier grid has shape (ny, nx), so a rectangular patch raises ValueError.

flatsky.radial_profile(z, xy=None, bin_size=1., minbin=0., maxbin=10., to_arcmins=1)

Average a 2-D field in annuli of constant radius.

Parameters:

  • z (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – Field to profile, real or complex. Must be 2-D when xy is not given.

  • xy (tuple of numpy.ndarray, optional) – Coordinate grids (x, y), each the same shape as z. Default is None, which uses numpy.indices(), i.e. pixel indices.

  • bin_size (float, optional) – Width of the radial bins, in the units of xy. Default is 1.

  • minbin (float, optional) – Lowest and highest radius of the binning. Defaults are 0 and 10.

  • maxbin (float, optional) – Lowest and highest radius of the binning. Defaults are 0 and 10.

  • to_arcmins (int, optional) – If non-zero, multiply the radius by 60 before binning, i.e. convert degrees to arcmin. Default is 1.

Returns:

radprf (numpy.ndarray) – Array of shape (nbin, 3) holding the bin center, the mean of z over the bin and an uncertainty.

Raises:

ValueError – If z is not 2-D and xy is not given or if the xy grids do not have the same shape as z.

Notes

The defaults are mutually inconsistent. to_arcmins presumes xy in degrees, whereas the fallback used when xy is omitted supplies pixel indices. Pass xy explicitly or set to_arcmins to zero, as map2cl() does.

The bin mean divides by the number of non-zero entries rather than by the number of entries, so a field containing exact zeros is averaged over its non-zero subset alone.

flatsky.map2cl(mapparams, flatskymap1, flatskymap2=None, binsize=None, minbin=100, maxbin=10000, mask=None, filter_2d=None)

Auto- or cross-power spectrum of one or two flat-sky maps.

The 2-D periodogram is formed and then averaged in annuli of \(\ell\) by radial_profile(),

\[\hat{C}_\ell = \frac{\mathrm{d}x^2}{n_x n_y} \left\langle \tilde{m}_1 \tilde{m}_2^* \right\rangle_\ell\, ,\]

where \(\mathrm{d}x\) is in radians and \(\tilde{m}\) is the unnormalized discrete transform.

Parameters:

  • mapparams (list) – Flat-sky map geometry [nx, ny, dx, dy].

  • flatskymap1 (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – First map, of shape (ny, nx).

  • flatskymap2 (numpy.typing.ArrayLike, optional) – Second map, of the same shape. If given, the cross spectrum is returned in place of the auto spectrum. Default is None.

  • binsize (float, optional) – Width of the \(\ell\) bins. Default is None, which uses the \(\ell_x\) grid spacing, i.e. along the second axis.

  • minbin (float, optional) – Lowest and highest \(\ell\) of the binning. Defaults are 100 and 10000.

  • maxbin (float, optional) – Lowest and highest \(\ell\) of the binning. Defaults are 100 and 10000.

  • mask (numpy.typing.ArrayLike, optional) – Window that the caller has already applied to the maps. Only its mean is used to rescale the spectrum. The maps are not multiplied by it here. Default is None.

  • filter_2d (numpy.typing.ArrayLike, optional) – Filter already applied to the maps, of shape (ny, nx). Its radial profile is divided out of the spectrum. Default is None.

Returns:

  • el (numpy.ndarray) – Bin centers.

  • cl (numpy.ndarray) – Binned power spectrum.

Raises:

ValueError – If flatskymap1 does not match the grid implied by mapparams or if flatskymap2 is given and does not have the same shape as flatskymap1.
